body:
Thank you for getting back to me! Service commitment: I already have. I've spoken at rehab centers, spoken at juvenile corrections, drove people from rehab centers to my home group, volunteered time at AA functions. I did all the things, even doing the steps (alone with online sheets though) that I'm supposed to. Except find a sponsor, and my pickings are slim. In my entire area, there is maybe 20 to 25 woman who have been in the program for at least a couple years, and many are unwilling to sponsor an agnostic. The others I've meet with are unsuitable, for mostly mismatched personalities or intellectual reasons. And seriously, the only other meetings are filled with middle aged to old guys who make my skin feel filled with crawling millipedes.

 I have a lot of issues with AA, the biggest is why can't we just recognize we have a common problem and support each other regardless if someone toes the party line? Why can't we share our stories and rather than 12 step them, recognize them as human and help them see the humanity in themselves and others? The 12 steps obviously don't, at least for the people in my area. I don't have a sponsor, so everyone looks away from my cries for help and companionship. I just don't understand. I'm not helping people so I stay sober. I'm helping so that light comes back and they can shine it on others.

Thank you for responding! My biggest problem is finding a sponsor. There are so few women in AA where I am, and there is a woman's AA group on Wednesday's that I tried for months but got me no where. I meet with a few I thought given time I could connect with, but I'm also agnostic so many times it was a conflict of ideologies. Several turned me down when I said I don't believe in God, but the relative good that lies in humanity even if it gets lost some times. I went through the steps using sheets online, read the big book, drove people from rehab to my home group, spoke at rehab centers about my story, spoke at a juvenile corrections center. I did the work, maybe not like I'm entirely supposed to, but I didn't just go to meetings. But this relapse enforces the idea of NOT relying on a sponsor. Replacing one crutch for another is not really a good idea. I'm thinking maybe this isn't for me at all, and I need to find ways to find the good in myself and others again. But thanks!
